We both asked if we'd be waiting much longer as the small child needed feeding and was getting tired waiting and it turns out we hadn't been checked in at all!

To get an appointment you have to ring up at 8am on the day you want it.
It's crazy, so everyone who wants an appointment is on the phone persistently redialing from 8am onwards. It took 157 redials to get through - not to a human, but to their queuing call system. That being said, after 18 minutes it then connected - but to another message, saying that they are migrating their systems over and cannot offer any non urgent appointments or issue repeat prescriptions, but to hold for urgent enquiries.

Why do their phone lines not give this information before 157 redials and 18 minutes on hold?

Anyway, I decided to hold and after some more music and waiting I actually spoke to a receptionist (08:42 - 42 minutes after first starting to contact them), who asked if it could "wait until tomorrow since I'd already waited three weeks" before trying to get this appointment. I explained that I didn't want to come running to doctor after 2 minutes as I wanted to see if my problem resolved itself and after three weeks it was time to try and get treatment.
I then explained that I had had to take time off work today just to try to get through to them as I couldn't commute in a car, constantly redialing, so I am now at home. I can't go through the same process again tomorrow, take time off work again and waste the morning trying to get through (to potentially not even get an appointment). But anyway through my persistence, I did secure an appointment.

Be aware though, there are previous occasions that I have got through after hundreds of redials - to then get told that all appointments have now been taken - try again tomorrow please.

This process needs a massive shake up, it is not fit for purpose. They used to have an online booking system (AskMyGP), which was fractionally better, but that you could only use it during certain working hours and was also hit and miss as whether you got an appointment. AskMyGP is no longer is use - so we are back to the 8am redial FreeForAll.

If you are looking at switching Doctors to this practice do not! They clearly do not have an appointment booking system fit for purpose, they clearly do not have enough receptionists to handle enquiries, they clearly have too many patients for the number of Doctors are if you have to work for a living....... Jeeze

Like a different reviewer previously said, I had to get a form completed by the doctors for my medical insurance.
